meta.source_system: DHCP client state-transition diagram, transcribed from RFC 2131 section 4.4 Figure 5, cross-checked against sections 3.1, 3.2 and 4.4.1-4.4.5. RFC 2131 is a public standard (proposed standard, March 1997).
meta.source_citation: RFC 2131 (March 1997), section 4.4, Figure 5 'State-transition diagram for DHCP clients'; sections 3.1, 3.2, 4.4.1-4.4.5 for cross-checks. Per-edge citations in meta.edges_with_citations.
action_names: DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2
T1 expires/Send DHCPREQUEST to leasing server
meta.semantics_class: event: the actions are protocol messages or timer events named by the figure labels; their names are part of the behavior and do not follow state renamings -- candidate groups in groups/ declare semantics "fixed". The relabel rows in expected.json are the diagnostic contrast reading, not the protocol-true one.
meta.encoding: states 8..15 = unreachable padding (self-loop only); undeclared (state, event) pairs self-loop with reward 0
meta.reward_rule: rewards all zero: DHCP defines no payoff; the reward layer carries no information, all conclusions come from the transition layer

transcription_notes: figure routing: RFC 2131's Figure 5 is a hand-drawn 1997 ASCII diagram; the exact routing of a few rails is ambiguous at pixel level (the two right-side rails into INIT labeled 'DHCPNAK/Halt network'; the discard self-loops). Where the drawing is ambiguous the edge endpoint is pinned by the section 3.1/3.2/4.4.x prose, which names the states explicitly; the figure label is kept verbatim as the event name.

prose-only edge: REQUESTING --DHCPNAK/Restart configuration--> INIT is stated in sec.3.1 step 5 but is not drawn in Figure 5; it is transcribed from prose and its label is prose-derived, not a figure-printed string. The twin edge INIT-REBOOT --DHCPNAK/Restart--> INIT IS drawn (and stated in sec.3.2).

right-side pair note: the figure prints 'DHCPNAK/Halt network' beside the far-right rail (from RENEWING) and 'DHCPNAK, Lease expired/Halt network' above REBINDING; sec.4.4.5 states the lease-expiry-to-INIT rule for BOTH RENEWING and REBINDING ('In both RENEWING and REBINDING states...' sec.4.4.5; 'If the lease expires before the client receives a DHCPACK, the client moves to INIT state'), so both INIT-transitions are RFC-supported regardless of which label is read onto which rail.

not collected: retransmission timeouts (sec.4.1 -- retransmits are self-loops with no state change; the encoding already maps undeclared events to self-loops, so they are not declared as actions); the 'silently discarded' stray-message rules of sec.4.4.1 beyond the two discard self-loops the figure actually draws (REQUESTING 'DHCPOFFER/Discard', BOUND 'DHCPOFFER, DHCPACK, DHCPNAK/Discard'); DHCPINFORM (the RFC itself remarks 'The DHCPINFORM message is not shown in figure 5', sec.4.4 intro).

encoding: states 8..15 are unreachable padding to reach 2^4 (engine input contract); any (state, event) pair not listed in EDGES self-loops with reward 0 (undeclared event = no state change); rewards are all zero because DHCP defines no payoff; goals is empty.

twin pair: RENEWING and REBINDING are the RFC's own conceptual twins (sec.4.4.5: both send DHCPREQUEST to extend the lease, differing in unicast vs broadcast and in T1 vs T2). Whether they are interchangeable as STATES is a question for the data -- see groups/renew_rebind.json and the case README. The twin edges they DO share verbatim: both leave on the identical label 'DHCPACK/Record lease, set timers T1, T2'.
